statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Nasdaq-100 futures have been halted since Friday's 21:00Z settlement, so no current price path exists to score. Friday's verified close was mid-range with VIX lower, and Tail remains in the low band.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping stays at EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The flagged window is the CME Globex reopen from 22:00Z on 27 September, where an unresolved Strait of Hormuz position meets the week's thinnest liquidity.
headline: Weekend halt keeps Tail low at 6; Hormuz rejection and a 5.18% 10-year frame the Sunday reopen
body: Nasdaq-100 futures have not traded since Friday 25 September settled at 21:00Z, so this assessment contains no live price-path evidence and says so explicitly. The newest verified tape is Friday's cash close: the Nasdaq-100 finished at 30,608.14, up 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and about 0.53% below the 30,770.63 52-week high, while the VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87. A mid-range close with declining implied volatility is a two-way auction, not the persistent no-retracement structure that Tail measures, which is why Tail sits at 6 despite a demanding macro backdrop. That backdrop is genuine and is carried in Stress at 54. The Federal Reserve raised rates at the 15-16 September meeting, the latest H.15 observation shows the 10-year at 5.18% and the 2-year at 4.87%, and the 10-year is close to its highest level in two decades with market pricing leaning toward a further increase in October. Equities absorbed that on Friday, with all three major indexes posting weekly gains. One weekend development is unresolved. WTI eased to about $92.41 on Friday, roughly 7.4% lower on the week, on optimism that the Strait of Hormuz might reopen; on Saturday that optimism was undercut when Iran's seven-day reopening proposal was rejected. Because no venue is quoting, that information cannot be priced until CME Globex reopens at 22:00Z on Sunday 27 September, which is the single flagged window in this publication and the final hour of the forecast. Shared Finviz context collected 13 minutes before this assessment is explicitly delayed latest-session data and its futures section was unavailable, so it is used only as confirmation: Technology rose 0.85%, Semiconductor Equipment & Materials 1.76%, and six of eight megacaps were higher, with MSFT up 3.66% and AAPL up 1.53% against META down 3.33% and TSLA down 1.54%. That internal rotation argues against index-level one-way structure. Confidence of 75 reflects verified levels, yields, oil, volatility and a full forward calendar set against price evidence that is now more than 26 hours old.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours span Friday's U.S. afternoon session and the weekend halt that followed. Published Tail fell from 10 to 6 as Friday's cash session closed mid-range and implied volatility declined, while Stress held between 44 and 54 on the rate backdrop and Confidence drifted from 86 down to 76 as price evidence aged past Friday's 21:00Z settlement. No hour in the window recorded persistent one-way structure or a failed retracement sequence.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are almost entirely a closed market: CME Globex equity-index futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday 27 September, the final slot of this forecast. Conditional Tail therefore stays in the low band, easing to 5 through the dead hours and rising gradually to 13 at the reopen, where an unresolved Strait of Hormuz position, oil that shed roughly 7.4% on the week, and a 10-year near a two-decade high meet the thinnest liquidity of the week. Stress runs between 51 and 60 on that backdrop and Confidence troughs near 66 before improving as live price discovery resumes. The escalation condition would be an initial gap that extends without meaningful retracement; an orderly two-way reopen would invalidate it.
